text:
Jordan: Quick thread 00 followup to the RFC: can we explore a client-hint-driven active-active cutover for tenant cohorts instead of snapshot-first? Idea: clients explicitly advertise consent + preferred region in SDK, we use that to steer reads/writes and gradually open writes on second region.
Priya: I'm skeptical. Client hints help steering but we still need a canonical reconciliation source. How do we guarantee auditability and legal proofs for gated tenants?
Mateo: Proposal: hybrid flow. Phase A: SDK adds `X-Region-Consent: eu-west=true;consent_ts=1670000000;sig=...`. Proxy verifies signature against tenant key and only then honors writes in eu-west. All writes include `consent_id` and `consent_sig` in event.
Ellen: That solves audit for consented writes. For gated (non-consent) tenants we reject client hints and continue control-plane-driven cutover. Keep both flows.
Jordan: Good. Operationally we need fast circuit-breakers on the serving side so if local capacity < threshold we return `429` with `x-error-code: REGION_OVERLOAD` and `x-retry-after`. No silent fallback.
Priya: Also add explicit SDK guidance: backoff jitter and an option `force_fallback=true` if tenant metadata allows fallback routing. SDK should expose region hint APIs.
Mateo: On reconciliation: rather than full key-level compare, stream write-ahead digests: write ops emit small per-shard HMACed digests every minute. Reconcile by comparing digests then drill down only if mismatch. Low IO.
Ellen: Ops note: digests must be reproducible and include `consent_id` and `snapshot_id` when applicable. Store digest manifests in audit bucket `s3://redwood-reconcile-manifests/`.
Jordan: Control-plane states still needed for non-consent paths. We'll add `active_active_allowed` flag per-tenant and `preferred_regions` list. Routing proxies cache this and fall back to reject if control-plane unreachable.
Priya: SLA: proxies should treat control-plane as MUST for gating; if it's >200ms p99 they degrade to reject for gated tenants. Track `control_plane_miss_ratio` per-proxy.
Mateo: Telemetry list for the experiment: per-tenant: writes_by_region, consented_write_ratio, digest_mismatch_rate, reconcile_drilldowns, rejected_writes(region_overload), average_write_e2e_latency, audit_manifest_emitted. Add a dashboard and a synthetic probe sending `X-Region-Consent` traffic.
Ellen: Add oncall alerting: page if digest_mismatch_rate > 0.05% sustained for 10m or if rejected_writes spikes > 1% of baseline.
Jordan: Rollout plan: 1) SDK flag opt-in for internal test apps. 2) Canary proxy changes with feature flag. 3) Run 6-hour synthetic test with 10k writes/minute. 4) Evaluate mismatch/dropped writes. 5) If stable, expand to small tenant cohort.
Priya: One more: legal wants a signed provenance file for each consented sequence: `provenance:{tenant}:{consent_id}:{window}.sig`. Must include public-key thumbprint, digest summary, and retention metadata.
Mateo: We'll generate provenance as part of the digest pipeline. Implementation detail: use `ed25519` signatures, store public key in tenant metadata service.
Ellen: Runbook excerpt (ops):
- Enable feature flag `client-hint-active-active` for test tenant.
- Monitor dashboard and check `audit_manifest_emitted` count.
- If digest_mismatch_rate > threshold -> flip `force_readonly` in control-plane and run reconciliation job.
- If region overloaded -> escalate to infra team and reduce traffic by toggling `client_hint_acceptance=false`.
ops-bot: heads-up: small canary deploy scheduled in 1h for proxy change. Job: proxy-canary-2026-03-21.
Jordan: Action items: Mateo implement digest emitter + provenance; Priya update SDK; Ellen add dashboard + alerts; I'll draft a brief consent spec for legal.
Priya: I'll also add SDK migration docs and a sample `X-Region-Consent` header generator for testing.
Mateo: I'll prototype digest format and sign-off tomorrow.
Ellen: I'll prepare the synthetic traffic harness and link results here.
Jordan: Thanks. Keep updates here and mark this thread `needs-runbook` when we're ready. :sparkles:
